Asked.description:
What the person is asked: what nothing on the TV recovers, as
`{ "step": … }`, with the person's next step for `ask`. Open: an app
reads a step it does not know as `ask` with `try_again`.

oneOf.description: The lights do not answer, and Prysm stopped trying.
The person must act, by this step.

fix.description: The person must act, by this step.

ErrorKind.description:
Why a call failed: the error reply's `errorKind`. `too_large`: the
payload exceeds 4096 bytes. `unknown_method`: no such method.
`forbidden`: only the TV app may change Prysm. `removing`: the service is
being removed. `invalid_request`: the payload is not the method's request.
`wrong_package`: the other package's method (`setTarget` on slim,
`setEnabled` on full). `invalid_preferences`: a preference the installed
package does not have. `save_failed`: the preferences could not be saved.
`internal`: the service could not read the call or send its reply. Open:
an app reads a kind it does not know as a refusal and shows `errorText`.

ErrorReply.description:
Any failed call. LS2's own replies (for example for a method that is not
registered) carry no `errorKind`; an app reads that as an unknown kind.

Fix.description:
The person's next step. `try_again`: start again. `change_settings`:
change the settings (in the portal); a save that validates replaces them.
`set_up`: set up the service again: it lacks a permission it needs.
`unsupported`: nothing makes this work on this TV. `restart_tv`: restart
the TV: a worker that did not end may still hold the capture. Open: an
app reads a fix it does not know as `try_again`.

FullWorker.description: The full package's worker process, as `{ "phase": … }`.

capturing.description:
Screen sync runs and frames arrive (false while it waits for
video).

fps.description:
Frames per second over about the last second, rounded, while
screen sync runs; 0 while it waits for frames.

lights.description:
Why the lights do not show what was chosen, as the worker last
reported it: with screen sync any issue, `unreachable` also while
it waits for lights that do not answer; with off or effects
`unreachable` alone, while the lights do not answer the request
that puts them in that mode (tried again until they do).

portal.description: The portal's LAN address once the worker reported it.

problem.description:
What the worker asks of the person: it keeps running, since its
portal is where settings change.

oneOf.description: Being stopped; the portal may still answer until it exits.

portal.description: The portal's LAN address the worker last reported.

problem.description:
What the person is asked once it exited; absent when a new
worker follows (a restart), or none is wanted.

oneOf.description:
No worker, and no portal: the person is asked. Choosing a target
(`setTarget`) answers it and starts the worker again.

subscribe.description: Keep sending the state on every change.

LightingTarget.description: What the user wants the LEDs to do.

OutputIssue.description:
Why the lights do not show what was chosen. `off`: the device is
switched off. `overridden`: the device's own override is on (WLED: live
override). `not_live`: the device is not taking the colours (WLED: not in
live mode, or no DDP arriving). `other_sender`: another sender's colours
reach the device. `unreachable`: the device does not answer Prysm's state
checks, the request that opens it for screen sync, or, with the target
`off` or `effects`, the request for that mode. During screen sync Prysm
keeps sending the colours; it tries an unanswered request again every few
seconds. The lights follow once the device takes the colours or answers.
Open: an app reads an issue it does not know in general words.

Package.description:
The installed package (both install as the same app), what the user asked
of it and its worker process, as `{ "flavor": … }`.

oneOf.description: `prysm-webos`: capture, processing, WLED and the portal on the TV.

target.description: The engine's target, including changes made in the portal.

oneOf.description: `prysm-webos-slim`: capture forwarded to a headless Prysm.

enabled.description: Frames should flow to the receiver.

Preferences.description:
The installed package's preferences: the `setPreferences` request
(complete, every field optional, an unset one absent) and the published
`preferences`. Fields marked "Slim only" must stay unset in the full
package. The file is [`PreferencesFile`].

autostart.description:
Start when the service starts: the full package starts screen sync,
the slim package streams to its receiver.

prysm_address.description:
Slim only: the headless Prysm's address, such as
`http://192.168.1.20:8787` or `https://prysm.example.com` (through a
reverse proxy). The TV streams its picture there, and the TV app
links to its portal. Only the syntax is checked when saved; the TV
resolves a host name at every connection attempt, and one that does
not resolve is reported as the receiver wait.

Problem.description: A failure the person is asked about.

enabled.description: Frames should flow to the receiver.

target.description: What the lights do: off, screen sync, or their own effects.

SlimLink.description:
Where the slim worker's stream to the receiver stands, as `{ "state": … }`.
`starting`: no connection attempt yet. `sending`: connected, frames go
out in `encoding` (the one the receiver requested, set in the desktop
portal), `fps` per second (0 while none come). `refused`: connected, but
the TV refuses to share the video it shows, so no frames go out; it ends
when the video changes, not a failure. `paused`: the
receiver stopped the stream because its lighting is off; the TV capture
is released until a receiver takes a connection again, not a failure.
`waiting`: the receiver is unavailable (not lighting, unreachable, or its
name does not resolve); the worker keeps reconnecting, not a failure.
`encoder_failed`: the encoder the receiver requested could not start or
failed; the receiver is told, and another encoding chosen in its portal
may work. `version_differs`: Prysm speaks another capture stream version;
the older one needs updating, and the worker keeps reconnecting.
`replaced`: another TV took over the stream at Prysm; this one sends no
more until capture is stopped and started, the TV wakes, or the Prysm
address changes. `receiver_failed`: Prysm's receiving source failed with
this TV's stream (a refusal, a keyframe that does not decode, no
decoder), and Prysm shows why; the worker released the capture and keeps
reconnecting. `message` says why, with the causes.

fps.description: Frames sent per second over about the last second, rounded.

SlimWorker.description: The slim package's worker process, as `{ "phase": … }`.

capturing.description:
Frames were sent in the last second (so also just after the
stream ended).

link.description:
Where the uplink to the receiver stands, as the worker last
reported it; it says the worker's own waits and failures.

problem.description:
What the person is asked once it exited; absent when a new
worker follows (a restart), or none is wanted.

oneOf.description:
No worker: the person is asked. Starting capture (`setEnabled`
true, also after stopping it) answers it and starts the worker
again.

log.description:
The latest log lines of the supervisor and the worker, oldest first
(at most 20).

unreadable.description:
Why the saved preferences could not be read: the service runs with
the defaults and keeps the file as it is until the app saves
preferences. Nothing stopped for it.

State.description:
The `getState` reply and subscription payload (plus LS2's `returnValue`):
the fields both packages have, and the installed package's own
([`Package`], tagged by `flavor`).

subscribed.description: On `getState` and subscription updates: whether the caller is subscribed.

StateReply.description: A successful state reply: [`State`] with LS2's `returnValue`.

StreamEncoding.description:
How the sender encodes the frames it sends: `h264_hardware`, the
sender's hardware H.264 encoder (the webOS TV's), about 2 Mbit/s;
`h264_software`, OpenH264 on the sender's CPU, about 2 Mbit/s; `raw`,
uncompressed NV12 pixels, about 21 Mbit/s at 320x180 and 30 fps. Exactly
this encoder is used: one that cannot start or fails stops the stream,
and the sender never switches to another.

Video.description:
The TV's main video output. Open: an app reads a value it does not know
as `unknown`.

info.description: The TV supervisor: Luna service, power and video gating, worker lifecycle, setup
info.title: Prysm TV service (luna://io.github.ericschaal.prysm.service)
